meta.exclusion_rule: For the outlier-excluded norm-Pearson metric (Step 2) and the outlier-excluded content-cosine metric (Step 3 variant): for each adjacent frame pair (i, i+1), a patch spatial position is excluded from the correlation/cosine average if it is among the top-k% highest-norm patches of EITHER frame i OR frame i+1 (union rule, not intersection). This is deliberately conservative -- it removes more patches than a per-frame-only or intersection-only rule -- specifically to avoid the residual bias where 'boring surviving votes agree because they are all background' could still occur if only one frame's outliers were masked. Top-k% is computed by count per frame (e.g. 256 patches at k=5% -> ceil(256*0.05)=13 patches masked), independently for each frame.
meta.kurtosis_definition: scipy.stats.kurtosis(fisher=True, bias=True) i.e. excess kurtosis (0 = normal dist).
meta.outlier_frac_definition: fraction of patches in a frame with norm > 3x that frame's median patch norm.
meta.position_stability_definition: For each sequence x encoder, take the flat-index set of the top-3 highest-norm patches in each of the 8 frames. Compare every frame's top-3 set against frame 0's top-3 set via (a) raw overlap count (0-3), (b) Jaccard index, (c) fraction of frames with >=1 shared position with frame 0, (d) fraction of frames with all 3 positions identical to frame 0, and (e) total number of unique positions that ever appear in any frame's top-3 (out of a max of 3*8=24 if no reuse at all; a low number close to 3 means the same few positions are chosen every frame -- i.e. spatially-fixed outlier tokens).
meta.content_cosine_definition: Raw per-patch D-dim feature vectors (post prefix/CLS-token removal, same tokens used for the norm-map metric) are L2-normalized and cosine similarity is computed independently at each spatial grid position between adjacent frames, then averaged over all patches, then averaged over the 7 adjacent pairs. This directly measures whether the CONTENT (direction) of a patch's feature vector is stable across time, independent of its norm -- so it should NOT be inflated by fixed-position high-norm outlier tokens whose direction may still vary, and conversely would reveal true temporal coherence the norm-only metric might miss.
meta.consistency_check_note: summary.orig_recomputed below recomputes the original (unexcluded) norm-Pearson metric from the SAME cached raw features used for all other metrics in this script, as an internal consistency check against temporal_scan_v3.json's original values (should match to float precision modulo any burst-index/frame-loading nondeterminism).

predictive_coherence.reason: Skipped per task instructions: reconstructing V-JEPA 2.1's predictor context/target mask sampling correctly outside the training pipeline is nontrivial (app.vjepa_2_1 predictor expects specific context/target block mask tensors generated by the training-time mask collator, not just raw encoder tokens), and hacking together an ad-hoc masking scheme risks producing a meaningless or misleading number. Steps 1-3 were prioritized and completed; Step 4 was explicitly marked optional/skippable in the task spec if uncertain.
